title: A smooth connected group scheme over an affine normal integral Noetherian base has an ample line bundle
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral affine Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-integral-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $H\to S$ be a smooth separated group scheme of finite presentation with geometrically connected fibres [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Here a group scheme means a group object in $S$-schemes, given by multiplication $H\times_SH\to H$, inverse $H\to H$ and unit $S\to H$ satisfying the group identities [def-pc-fibre-product]; commutativity is not required. Then there exists an ample invertible $\mathcal O_H$-module on all of $H$ [def-sc-invertible-module] [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. In particular the conclusion is global over the given affine integral base, not merely the existence of an open cover of $S$ on which ample modules exist.

source.place: Corollary 6.14, printed p.19, version March 31, 2026, especially its affine integral base conclusion, applied to the homogeneous scheme X=H for left translation. https://ningguomath.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/amplenew-1.pdf . WANTED local copy.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normal-group-affine-fibre-transversal] to the given $H\to S$. Its hypotheses are exactly the assumed normal integral affine Noetherian base and smooth separated finitely presented group with geometrically connected fibres. Obtain an affine open $V\subseteq H$ with $V_s\ne\varnothing$ for every $s\in S$. This is a global geometric input; choosing an affine chart near one unit point and shrinking the base would not give it.

source.place: Corollary 6.14, affine integral base clause; global geometric input isolated as an unsplit prerequisite.

proof.text: Finite presentation gives quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-section-component-geometrically-irreducible] to $H\to S$ and its unit section $e$. Its open $W\subseteq H$ contains every point in the fibre connected component through $e(s)$. Each $H_s$ is connected and contains $e(s)$, so this component is the entire fibre. Therefore $W=H$ and every $H_s$ is geometrically irreducible, in particular irreducible. The nonempty open $V_s$ is dense: if a nonempty open missed it, the two disjoint nonempty opens would contradict irreducibility.

source.place: Fibrewise density for the boundary construction, as in Corollary 6.13; smooth section-component theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-normal-affine-boundary-cartier] with $T=S$, $X=H$, $U=V$. An affine Noetherian base is locally Noetherian, and its normal local-ring hypothesis is the one assumed here. Smoothness, separatedness and finite presentation are given; $V$ is affine by step 1 and dense in every fibre by step 2. Hence the reduced boundary $D=(H\setminus V)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is an effective Cartier divisor, with support exactly $H\setminus V$. The lemma includes the empty boundary.

source.place: Proposition 3.3 and Theorem 6.8, boundary-divisor construction in the Noetherian specialization.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal I_D$ for the ideal of $D$. It is invertible by [lemma-nagata-effective-cartier-is-invertible]. Set $L=\mathcal I_D^\vee=\mathcal O_H(D)$ as in [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]; the dual of a local free rank-one module is again free of rank one [def-sc-invertible-module]. The inclusion $\mathcal I_D\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_H$ is a global section $\sigma$ of $L$. Locally, if $\mathcal I_D=f\mathcal O_H$, the dual frame taking $f$ to $1$ represents $\sigma$ by $f$. Thus its residue value is nonzero exactly off $D$, so $H_\sigma=V$, using the section-locus definition [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. The local sections agree since they express the same inclusion.

source.place: Theorem 6.8, step 3; local calculation of the canonical divisor section, written explicitly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-group-affine-section-ampleness] to $H\to S$, $L$, $n=1$ and $\sigma$. The base is affine normal locally Noetherian; the group is smooth separated finitely presented, and geometric connectedness implies connectedness of its fibres. Step 4 gives the affine section locus $H_\sigma=V$, and step 1 says it meets every fibre. The criterion concludes that $L$ is ample in the absolute sense on all of $H$. No base restriction or commutativity hypothesis has entered.

source.place: Proposition 5.9 and Corollary 6.6(ii), supplied-section criterion, yielding Corollary 6.14 for left translation.

proof_origin.place: Corollary 6.14 affine integral base clause, assembled from the boundary construction of Proposition 3.3/Theorem 6.8 and the supplied-section criterion; the global affine-transversal reduction is explicitly left as a new unsplit node.

Guo's Thm 6.8 makes O(D) S-ample once there is one S-quasi-affine U with G·U=X. Cor 6.14(ii) obtains U only 'by localization on S', so its global affine-integral clause rests exactly on the input the delivery isolates as the new node (D5 handled correctly; the report honestly says the node is agent-formulated). Item statement unchanged. Step 1 cites the new node with the same hypotheses. Step 2 uses the smooth-section-component node (qcqs from finite presentation, unit section): the open is all of H, so the fibres are irreducible and V_s is dense. Step 3 checks every hypothesis of the boundary-cartier node (affine normal locally Noetherian base; smooth, separated, finitely presented; V affine and fibrewise dense) and gets D=(H\V)_red effective Cartier. Step 4 is elementary: L=I_D^dual, sigma the inclusion, coefficient f in the dual frame, H_sigma=V; same calculation as the reviewed local node. Step 5 checks every hypothesis of group-affine-section-ampleness (n=1, affine H_sigma meeting every fibre) and concludes absolute ampleness. The new node satisfies B1-B4/B7, its searches are recorded, and rg -L finds no duplicate (the local node only shrinks the base). It is not a restatement: it asserts no line bundle, ampleness needs the Ramanujam-Samuel and square-action nodes, and the converse needs hypersurface avoidance (Gabber-Liu-Lorenzini type, not in the DAG). Small cases hold: H=S (relative dimension 0), affine H (V=H), an elliptic curve over a Dedekind ring (V=E minus the zero section), constant proper H0×S; it is true whenever the item is. Maintainer note: the source gives no global construction, so whoever splits the node must supply one (Raynaud VI WANTED) and must not cite back to the item. Accepted tool_uses: lem-sbc-smooth-section-component-geometrically-irreducible and lemma-nagata-effective-cartier-is-invertible, both generic.
